text: The evening sea was calm and silver-blue.
Sunny watched the water from the pier.
And suddenly, a smooth and shining back
curved up out of the water like a wave!
A dolphin! With a smile built into her face,
and eyes that sparkled brighter than the sea.
“Hello!” she clicked. “I'm on my evening swim!
One last happy lap before I rest!”
She leapt and made a rainbow out of spray,
then landed with the gentlest of splashes.
“But how do dolphins sleep?” asked Sunny, wondering.
“You cannot lie down in the rolling sea!”
“We sleep while swimming slow,” the dolphin smiled.
“Half of me stays up to steer me safe.”
“One eye sleeps first, and then the other follows.
The sea rocks me the way it rocks the boats.”
She swam a slow and dreamy figure-eight,
her splashing softer now, her leaps all done.
Then off she glided, gentle as the tide,
one bright eye already lost in dreams.
Sunny curled up in a coil of rope,
still warm and smelling of the summer sun.
The bay was still. The little waves said hush.
Everything was peaceful, deep, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy with the rocking water.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept above the sleeping sea,
dreaming half-awake the way that dolphins do.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, smiling dolphin.
Goodnight, rocking sea. Goodnight, little one.
